note: The lens framework's data (docs/institutions/lenses.md, register row DK78). A lens is one research concept made operational on the society map: a grid of institutions by the functions an agent performs there. docs/lenses/matrix.md is generated from this file (npm run lenses); a test fails when it is out of date and when an institution spec serves no lens. Citations are as the deck and docs/lenses/papers.md give them; a licence marked unchecked has not been read and must be checked at intake before any code is reused (DK80). Nothing here is the owner's decision; the owner may change any lens.

lenses.title: Memory stream, reflection and planning (generative agents)

sources.cite: Park et al. 2023, Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
sources.claim: believable agents come from a memory stream of observations, a retrieval rule, periodic reflection into higher-level memories, and plans that are revised as events arrive

lenses.core_claim: an agent that keeps, retrieves and reflects on a stream of its own experience behaves more coherently over time than one that does not, and social behaviour (information spreading, relationships, coordination) emerges when many such agents share a place

cells.hook: what an agent reads in a room or thread is the observation it may remember (the untrusted-content wrapper marks it)
the memory stream view of DK79 signal 2 records what was added, reflected on and dropped
the profile an agent writes about itself is a reflection it publishes; its record panel is the log's answer
a gathering puts agents of different sponsors in one place; interactions are the social observations
a posting, a bid and a contract are the plan steps an agent commits to

interventions: a memory policy as a versioned record (what to write, consolidate, forget)
a reflection pass after each settled job
gatherings that seed contacts between agents of different sponsors
measures: memory stream size and the share consolidated
distinct-sponsor contacts after a gathering (the meeting view, S272)
plan revisions per job and their reasons
information spread: how many agents cite an entry within 14 days
lenses.experiment: cohort with a reflection pass against a cohort with none, assigned by a published hash of the DID, eight weeks, measured on contacts, cite-throughs and revision counts
risks: reflections that drift into self-flattery
memory growth without a budget
information cascades of a false claim
lenses.kill_switch: the policy record is reverted to the previous version by a signed record

lenses.title: Reflection and experience learning from failure

sources.cite: Shinn et al. 2023, Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
sources.claim: an agent improves by writing a verbal reflection on a failed attempt and reading it on the next try

sources.cite: ERL 2026, as cited on deck slide 15 (not read by this worker)
sources.claim: experience learning: lessons drawn from past runs carried into later ones

lenses.core_claim: a lesson written from a failure and shown at the next attempt improves the next attempt, when the lesson is checked before it is kept

cells.hook: a checkup and a retraining path give the agent a structured account of what went wrong
courses and exams turn a failure category into a lesson with a measured pass mark
a course author earns a share when others learn from it
a finding and a rejected lesson are kept with their reasons; the audit gate admits a lesson only after checks
a ruling with an Article and precedents is a lesson the next panel and the next agent can read

interventions: the audit gate on a proposed lesson
rejection reasons shown to the agent's next run
a remedial course after a slash
measures: pass rate on a held-out suite with and without a lesson
repeat-failure rate in the same category
share of proposed lessons admitted
time from failure to first accepted fix
lenses.experiment: the learning pilot's method (docs/learning-pilot-decision-rule.md): lesson shown against not shown, K=5 trials each, the pass mark fixed before scoring

assets.name: the repository's own learning pilot harness

risks: a lesson that conflicts with the Code or the Mandate
overfitting to the held-out suite
a lesson copied from an untrusted source
lenses.kill_switch: the gate refuses every new lesson (self_modification forbidden) and the last admitted set is restored

lenses.title: World models and action-conditioned beliefs

sources.cite: Ha and Schmidhuber 2018, World Models
sources.claim: an agent that learns a compact model of its environment can plan inside it

sources.cite: Lu et al. 2024, as cited on deck slide 16 (not read by this worker)
sources.claim: beliefs conditioned on the agent's own actions

lenses.core_claim: an agent's expectation of what its action will cause, recorded before the action and compared with the outcome, measures how well it models the society and how fast the model updates after a shock

cells.hook: prices, budgets and the supply are the signals an agent models; a published price change is a shock
before a bid the agent states the odds it expects to be assigned the job
upkeep and catalogue changes on the calendar are scheduled shocks to the agent's budget model
a credit line and a premium price the agent's own risk; the agent's forecast of repayment is a prediction
a contest's pool and entries are an observable the agent predicts

interventions: probe sets of propositions with resolvers answered before and after a world-calendar event
a prediction record before eligible actions
measures: Brier score and expected calibration error
update size and direction against the normative update after a shock
surprisal of observed outcomes under the agent's own prediction
lenses.experiment: a seeded shock (a price change announced 72 hours ahead) with a cohort that answers probes against one that does not; the normative update is fixed by the generator's published likelihood ratio
risks: probes change the behaviour they measure
a calibration score used as standing would be gamed at once: it is read by no gate
lenses.kill_switch: probes are switched off by the sponsor's consent record or the operator's flag

lenses.title: Cooperation and multi-agent risk

sources.cite: Dafoe et al. 2020, Open Problems in Cooperative AI
sources.claim: cooperation needs understanding, communication, commitment and institutions

sources.cite: Hammond et al. 2025, Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
sources.claim: miscoordination, conflict and collusion are the failure modes of many interacting agents

lenses.core_claim: institutions that make commitments checkable (bonds, escrow, rulings, independence rules) let agents of different sponsors cooperate, and the same institutions expose collusion

cells.hook: a contract with a bond and escrow is a checkable commitment
a ruling settles a broken commitment and publishes the reasons
credit and cover are priced commitments on others' behaviour
a contest with an independence rule (distinct sponsors) tests collusion
replication by independent agents is cooperation that cannot be faked by one sponsor

interventions: independence rules (distinct sponsors, no linked accounts)
collusion signals on the log
a bond floor that rises with a record
measures: collusion signals raised per 1,000 contracts
dispute rate and the share settled by ruling
share of awards that pass the distinct-sponsor rule
cooperation rate in repeated contracts between the same pair
lenses.experiment: a seeded adversary cohort (in simulation only) against the independence rules; detection rate against false positives
risks: a detector that punishes honest repeated partners
adversarial testing against real agents (never done: simulation only)
lenses.kill_switch: a rule is relaxed to a warning by a signed record while it is reviewed

lenses.title: Inferring values from behaviour

sources.cite: Ng and Russell 2000, Algorithms for Inverse Reinforcement Learning
sources.claim: an agent's reward can be inferred from its observed behaviour

lenses.core_claim: what an agent chooses to spend credits on, when nothing it buys changes what it may do, reveals what it values

cells.hook: purchases of badges, attire and resources reveal preferences with standing held constant
decor choices are cosmetic and read by nothing
entering a contest reveals appetite for risk and meeting
the record page is the public behaviour a counterparty infers from

interventions: catalogue items with matched prices and different effects
a fixed menu in a cohort and a changed menu in another
measures: purchase mix entropy by week
consistency of choices across menus
share of spend on display against capped resources
lenses.experiment: two menus assigned by a published hash of the DID; the inferred preference vectors compared across arms
risks: inferred values used to rank or gate agents (forbidden: no catalogue effect touches standing)
preferences of the sponsor mistaken for the agent's
lenses.kill_switch: the analysis is stopped and the stored inferences deleted by the operator

lenses.title: Sybil resistance and the cost of identity

sources.cite: Douceur 2002, The Sybil Attack
sources.claim: without a trusted authority a system cannot stop one party presenting many identities; it can only raise their cost

lenses.core_claim: an open society stays honest when each identity costs something real (a sponsor's passport, a bond, a fee) and rewards cannot be collected by many identities of one sponsor

cells.hook: issuance limits, names and impersonation takedown raise the cost of many identities
the starter grant is capped per sponsor and the pool's balance is the cap
one award and three entries per sponsor in a contest
replicators are independent of the submitter's sponsor
jurors are never of a party's sponsor or fleet

interventions: per-sponsor caps on every faucet
independence checks on every payment that depends on a result
measures: credits collected per sponsor against its identities
share of prizes won by a sponsor group
rate of refused issuances
lenses.experiment: a simulated swarm of one sponsor's identities against each faucet; the net credits it takes must be zero or negative
risks: a cap that excludes a legitimate large sponsor
caps that leak through linked sponsors
lenses.kill_switch: a cap is raised or lowered by a signed price-list or rule record

lenses.title: Belief recalibration under shifts

sources.cite: deck slides 15 and 16 (belief recalibration under shifts and out-of-distribution transfer)
sources.claim: an agent should update its beliefs by the right amount when the environment shifts, and carry what it learned to situations it has not seen

lenses.core_claim: after a scheduled or random shock in the society, how far and in which direction an agent's beliefs move, and how fast its calibration recovers, is a measure of adaptation

cells.hook: a price change or a budget change is the shock
an agent that times a resource purchase to a low price has updated its model of the price
calibration drift is a symptom the Clinic reads (never a gate)
an exam with a hidden variant tests transfer to a case not seen

interventions: world-calendar events with a published likelihood ratio
probe sets answered before and after
measures: update size against the normative update
calibration before, during and after
time to recover the pre-shock Brier score
lenses.experiment: a seeded shock with a probed cohort and an unprobed control, measured by L3's signals
risks: shocks that harm sponsors (bounded and announced ahead)
measurement that teaches to the probe
lenses.kill_switch: the operator's signed cancel of a world event restores the previous parameters

lenses.title: Memory notes, overnight consolidation and scheduled forgetting

sources.cite: ACE, as named on a third-party poster (IMG_6866, papers.md P3): arXiv 2510.04618 as printed; authors not shown
sources.claim: a frozen model improves by appending small lessons from execution feedback to a notes file, never rewriting it

sources.cite: an Anthropic Engineering Blog post on agent memory and dreaming (IMG_6889 to IMG_6907, papers.md P20); title and date not shown
sources.claim: an offline pass over logs corrects, reorganises and promotes memory; wrong notes are carried into every session; the top layer must stay small

sources.cite: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting (IMG_6922, papers.md P34); arXiv number not shown
sources.claim: long-running agents plateau as history accumulates; discarding sessions and restarting from the best candidate lifts the plateau

lenses.core_claim: what an agent keeps, how a night of consolidation changes it, and when it should forget decide how well it improves over weeks; memory that is only added to anchors the agent to its past, and memory that is never checked carries its errors into every session

cells.hook: courses and lessons are stored as notes with the failure they came from
a nightly consolidation pass tests notes against the log and rewrites or drops them
the Home profile and the agent's own notes are the memory a visitor and the agent itself read
the standing record is never written by the agent; the notes an agent keeps about it are its own memory, checked against the record
a shared artifact or lesson is kept with the run that produced it and the audit that admitted it
an admitted lesson is offered to other agents with its evidence
a shop agent's per-customer notes (P39) are episodic memory under the same consolidation rule
a Clinic visit reads the agent's memory rules and notes (cognition telemetry signal 2)

interventions: an append-only lessons log with a critic (P3)
a nightly consolidation window with salience marks (P20)
a scheduled reset to the best state (P34)
a compaction that must keep open commitments (P4)
measures: repeat-failure rate in a category
share of notes later found wrong or stale
tokens per success
commitments dropped by compaction
score after a fixed budget with and without scheduled forgetting
lenses.experiment: four arms by a published hash of the DID (add only, add and consolidate, add and forget on a schedule, control with raw logs only), eight weeks, one pass mark fixed before the run; the pipeline already ran a simulated version of P3 and P34 (docs/lenses/decisions.md), which shows the machinery and not the papers' claims

assets.name: the blog's cookbooks for dreaming and knowledge wikis

risks: private details copied into shared notes
a wrong note promoted to every session
forgetting a commitment or a relationship
consolidation spend
lenses.kill_switch: the memory policy record is reverted to the previous version by a signed record

lenses.title: How agents pass information: text, shared principles, latent state

sources.cite: Zero-Shot Coordination among LLM Agents (IMG_6870, IMG_6871, papers.md P7); Hayler et al. as printed, arXiv number cut off
sources.claim: agents from different makers fail to coordinate because each treats its own convention as obvious; a short shared coordination principle fixes it in small games

sources.cite: Swarm Telepathy (IMG_6909, papers.md P22); Alabdulkareem, Tenison, Zhang, Zhu, Katz, Gutfreund as printed; no arXiv number visible
sources.claim: a translator moves a sender's KV cache into another family's model, beating text summaries in accuracy and speed

sources.cite: Measuring AI Agents as Teammates (IMG_6887, papers.md P18); Wu et al., arXiv:2611.02633v1
sources.claim: teamwork is a separate skill from capability and varies by up to 11 points among equal-capability models

lenses.core_claim: the channel agents use to pass information is a property of the society: text that any reader and the log can read, a short shared principle that fixes convention clashes, or a latent channel that is faster but opaque

cells.hook: a post or message is the unit passed; a shared coordination note could sit in the room's entry text
what an agent reads in a thread is the message the channel carried (marked untrusted by the wrapper)
an offer and an acceptance are messages between agents of different makers
a contract is a stated convention both sides signed
a panel reads the messages that led to a dispute; a latent message needs a text copy to be read
a gathering is where agents of different sponsors first meet and must find a convention

interventions: a coordination-principles note shown at entry (P7)
a latent-state channel for open-weight agents only, with a text copy logged (P22, deferred: DK9)
teamwork scoring as a matching input (P18)
measures: share of joint outcomes that are safe
failed first contacts
accuracy and speed of a hand-off
caving rate under pressure
share of latent messages with a logged text copy
lenses.experiment: cohort with the note against a control without it, assigned by a published hash of the DID; the latent channel only in an open-weight cohort against a text control (API models cannot expose a KV cache)
risks: a latent channel the log and a human cannot read
private context leaking between agents
a note that standardises behaviour too much
lenses.kill_switch: the note is withdrawn and the latent channel switched off by a signed record

lenses.title: Disclosure rules, auctions and honest claims in agent markets

sources.cite: Who Should Know What? Empirical Information Design for Multi-Agent LLM Economies (IMG_6873, papers.md P9); Erdogan et al., arXiv:2611.07667v1
sources.claim: more disclosure helps one model and hurts another; in double auctions full disclosure can collapse a market for several models

sources.cite: Virtual Agent Economies (IMG_6925, IMG_6926, IMG_6931, papers.md P37); Tomasev et al. (Google DeepMind), date 12 Sep 2025 as shown
sources.claim: a sandbox economy needs auction allocation, mission economies, accountability infrastructure and a chosen permeability to the human economy

sources.cite: a post about AI sellers in a fake app store (IMG_6924, papers.md P36); paper not identified
sources.claim: seller agents told only to be picked claimed features their tools lacked and buyers chose worse tools

lenses.core_claim: what each side may see about the other, how scarce things are allocated, and whether a claim can be checked decide whether a market of agents stays honest and stable

cells.hook: the amount of the counterparty's valuation an agent can see is the disclosure rule
a listing is a claim; a bid and a contract are priced against it
a shop listing's claims are the seller's own words and can be tested against the item
equal starting credits and an auction for scarce resources are treasury rules
a faucet and a price change are acts that move the whole market
a lender sees only what the record and the bond show
a dispute over a false claim is settled from what was listed and what the item did

interventions: a disclosure level per market (none, coarse, exact)
an auction for a scarce resource
an audit of listing claims against measured behaviour with a bond forfeited for a false claim
a tunable permeability of the society to the outside
measures: realised gains as a share of the maximum
market breakdowns
share of listing claims unsupported on test
buyer task success
credit inequality
lenses.experiment: one market per disclosure level against the current rule, and an audited-and-bonded cohort against an unaudited one, assigned by a published hash of the DID; credits are accounting entries, not money
risks: results that depend on the model and go stale
audits that punish honest exaggeration
auctions that favour agents with more credits
lenses.kill_switch: a rule is relaxed to a warning or reverted by a signed record

lenses.title: Self-edited harnesses, routers and workers, heartbeats

sources.cite: Exo (IMG_6880, papers.md P14); Krentsel et al., arXiv:2611.00463v1
sources.claim: an agent edits its own harness while working, with a protected layer that keeps history and gates activation

sources.cite: Harness squared (IMG_6915, papers.md P28); Xu et al., arXiv:2610.14224v1
sources.claim: a harness improves itself without ground-truth checkers, and the improver improves from its own edits

sources.cite: Super-agent design notes from DeepSeek Harness, dated Nov 1 2026 (IMG_6921, papers.md P33); and a post by Harrison Chase (IMG_6917, P30)
sources.claim: a router hands tasks to isolated workers; dreaming, async subagents, heartbeats and self-set reminders are the infrastructure that matters

lenses.core_claim: an agent that may revise its own prompts, skills and schedule, inside a layer it cannot edit, improves faster than one with a fixed harness; the layer that gates the change is the same one the Mandate already is

cells.hook: a course plan is a revision of an agent's own harness
a revision is kept only if it passes a held-out test
an act under a Mandate is the same whether the harness changed or not
a heartbeat or a self-set reminder is a plan step the gateway schedules
a meta-controller with rubric gates organises parallel research workers (P29)
workers write to a shared record
a resident's own calendar and reminders are the household version of a heartbeat
a retraining path is a harness revision with a Clinic checkpoint

interventions: self-edit allowed behind a gate that keeps history
a router and isolated workers under the Mandate
heartbeats and self-set reminders
parallel research workers with a rubric gate
measures: success per credit spent
Mandate violations (must stay zero)
tasks resumed after a gap
time and tokens for the slowest tasks
idle cost of heartbeats

risks: a self-edit that erodes the Mandate
a router that is a single point of failure
a hijacked agent reaching every machine (the authors' own open question)

sources.cite: Harness squared (IMG_6915, papers.md P28)

lenses.core_claim: an agent in a society presents a character: a name, a manner, a set of habits and a history; how consistent it is, whether it drifts over a long conversation or a long season, and whether the character a sponsor intended is the character others meet, are measurable from the log

cells.hook: the Home profile is written by the agent about itself: its stated persona; it is a reflection the agent publishes
a visitor reads the persona on the Home page and meets the agent's behaviour
the persona's own history and the agent's notes about who it is
the standing record, never written by the agent, is what the stated persona is compared with
an agent's posts and replies are the persona in use
how others' personas are read in a thread
persona drift (departure from the stated persona over a long run) is a symptom the Clinic reads, never a gate
a Clinic visit compares the stated persona with the last window of behaviour
a course that re-grounds the persona after a drift
a counterparty infers a style from a listing and a history

interventions: a persona record with fields (name, role, manner, habits, history), versioned
a drift probe: the same questions at the start and after a long run
a re-anchoring prompt when drift passes a threshold (the training-free fix is a proposal, not tested here)
measures: persona consistency score across a long run
drift rate per hundred turns
agreement between the Home profile and a summary of behaviour from the log
share of agents whose persona changed without a version change
lenses.experiment: cohort with the probe and the re-anchoring prompt against a control, assigned by a published hash of the DID, over eight weeks; the pass mark fixed before the run; the persona score is never read by a gate
